support_spans: high titers of ANA, anti–double-stranded DNA, and anti–Smith antibodies
low complement C3 levels
urinalysis showed pH 5, 16 WBCs and 27 RBCs per high-power field
contradict_spans: CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis and an axillary lymph node biopsy were negative for malignancy
concepts.why: The presence of high titers of ANA, anti–double-stranded DNA, and anti–Smith antibodies, along with low complement C3 levels, is unusual and points towards Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.

support_spans: non–anion gap metabolic acidosis with hyperkalemia
morning serum aldosterone was less than 1 ng/dL
contradict_spans: The patient had been noncompliant with her hypertension medication, lisinopril, for over three years, which could contribute to her hyperkalemia
concepts.why: The presence of non–anion gap metabolic acidosis with hyperkalemia, along with a morning serum aldosterone level less than 1 ng/dL, is unusual and points towards Addison's Disease.

support_spans: mucosal pallor and non-tender, rubbery axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy
contradict_spans: CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis and an axillary lymph node biopsy were negative for malignancy
concepts.why: The presence of non-tender, rubbery axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy is unusual and could be indicative of Lymphoma, although the negative biopsy results argue against it.

support_spans: high titers of ANA
contradict_spans: The patient did not have any symptoms of dry eyes or dry mouth, which are common in Sjögren's Syndrome
concepts.why: The presence of high titers of ANA could be indicative of Sjögren's Syndrome, although the lack of symptoms of dry eyes or dry mouth argues against it.

support_spans: high titers of ANA, anti–double-stranded DNA, and anti–Smith antibodies
low complement C3 levels
contradict_spans: The patient did not have any symptoms of sclerodactyly or esophageal dysmotility, which are common in MCTD
concepts.why: The presence of high titers of ANA, anti–double-stranded DNA, and anti–Smith antibodies, along with low complement C3 levels, could be indicative of Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, although the lack of symptoms of sclerodactyly or esophageal dysmotility argues against it.
